asymmetry

/ay-SIM-uh-tree/ - the stress falls on SIM · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Asymmetry means a lack of balance or matching between two sides or parts — one side differs from the other in size, shape, or share.

Economists blame the used-car market's troubles on an asymmetry of information: the seller knows the car's history, and the buyer knows the paint.

Example

Reviewing the bridge's sensor data, the engineer flagged a slight asymmetry: the east cable was carrying four percent more load than the west, though the design called for a perfect split.

Nothing is broken yet — four percent is small — but the two sides that should mirror each other don't, and that mismatch is what asymmetry names. Greek a- ('not') joins symmetria ('measuring together'), so the meaning is built right into the word: the sides no longer measure alike.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

imbalance: Imbalance means unequal weight or force between two things; asymmetry is the more precise, technical cousin — it points at the mismatch itself, one side measured against the other.

lopsidedness: Lopsidedness means leaning visibly to one side; lopsidedness is what asymmetry looks like from across the room — the casual word for a fault grown obvious.

disparity: Disparity means a great difference between amounts or levels, usually of resources or outcomes; asymmetry can be tiny — a millimeter's difference is still asymmetry, while disparity implies a gap that matters.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

symmetry: both sides matching each other exactly

evenness: the same in measure or share throughout

Where it sits · how badly the two sides fail to match

unevenness → asymmetry → lopsidedness

unevenness vs. asymmetry: Unevenness is milder than asymmetry: a surface can be slightly uneven anywhere, while asymmetry indicts the design itself — side measured against side, and failing the comparison.

lopsidedness vs. asymmetry: Lopsidedness is asymmetry grown severe and obvious: nobody needs calipers, because the whole shape visibly heels to one side.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-: not, without (Greek)

Prefix — sym-: together (Greek syn-)

Root — metr-: measure (Greek metron)

Suffix — -y: state or quality of

Put it together: Read it off the pieces: a- ('not') + sym- ('together') + metron ('measure') + -y — the state of not measuring together. Metron is one of Greek's busiest exports to English; it hides inside every -meter word science owns.

Use the root in a new word: perimeter: The guards walked the fort's perimeter twice each night, lanterns swinging in the dark.

Root Check

Word Choice

precise / analytical

Asymmetry is the measurer's word for a mismatch — cool, exact, and at home in science and argument alike: asymmetries of information, of power, of load. Use lopsided when you want the reader to see the tilt; use asymmetry when you want them to check the numbers.
